# Which system of employment law applies

Two systems of employment law operate for the private sector in WA and which system covers you depends on the employer’s business structure.

Last updated: 26 October 2026

## Contents

1. [State system](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/which-system-of-employment-law-applies#state-system)
2. [National system](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/which-system-of-employment-law-applies#national-system)
3. [Checking system coverage](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/which-system-of-employment-law-applies#checking-system-coverage)
4. [Related services and information](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/which-system-of-employment-law-applies#rel-services-01)

Contents1 - State system2 - National system3 - Checking system coverage4 - Related services and information

Two systems of employment law operate for the private sector in Western Australia:

- the state industrial relations system (state system); and
- the national fair work system (national system).

Working out which system covers an employer and its employees is the first step in understanding and complying with employment rights and obligations and this depends on the employer’s business structure.

> [Watch our video on which system of employment law applies](https://vimeo.com/844772912)

## State system

### Private sector businesses, not-for-profit organisations, and household employers

The state system covers:

- Private sector businesses and their employees that operate as:
  - Sole traders.
  - Partnerships, where none of the partners in the business is a constitutional corporation (trading or financial corporation).
  - Trust arrangements, where none of the trustees operating the business is a constitutional corporation (trading or financial corporation).

> Note - Incorporated employers in the private sector, including Pty Ltd entities, who sell goods or provide services for a fee may satisfy the criteria of a trading or financial corporation.

- Individuals who are household employers who personally and directly employ someone to provide domestic services in a private home, and their employees.
- Incorporated associations and other not-for-profit organisations, including some sporting clubs and school P&C's, which are not constitutional corporations (trading or financial corporations) and their employees.
  - A not-for-profit association may be a constitutional corporation (and therefore in the national system) if it has sufficiently substantial trading or financial activities, even if the purpose of the organisation is something other than trading or finance or if it receives government funding. Trading activities typically involve buying or selling and produce revenue for the organisation. Financial activities often involve the borrowing of money and the provision of finance.
  - There is no definitive rule on which system covers these types of organisations and each organisation will need to seek its own legal advice to determine this question as Wageline is not able to advise on this issue.

Information for private sector state system employers and employees is available at:

- [Finding the right pay rate](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/finding-the-right-pay-rate "")
- [WA award summaries](https://www.wa.gov.au/service/employment/employment-and-industrial-relations-matters/wa-award-summaries "")
- [Long service leave](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/long-service-leave-western-australia "Long service leave in Western Australia")
- [Annual, personal and other leave](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/annual-personal-leave-and-other-leave-state-system-employees "Annual, personal leave and other leave for state system employees")
- [When employment ends](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/when-employment-ends-state-system-employees "When employment ends for state system employees")

Private sector state system employers and employees can call Wageline on 1300 655 266 about pay rates, leave and employment issues.

For information on child employment laws visit [When children can work in Western Australia](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/when-children-can-work-western-australia "") or call Wageline on 1300 655 266.

### Local Government

All Western Australian local government employers and employees are covered by the state system.

Local government employers may have industrial (enterprise) agreements that provide pay and entitlements specific to their workforce. Contact the Human Resources area of the local government for information on any relevant industrial agreement.

WA award summaries are available for the two main local government state awards, the [Local Government Officers (Western Australia) Award](https://www.wa.gov.au/government/publications/local-government-officers-award-summary "Local Government Officers Award summary") and the [Municipal Employees (Western Australia) Award](https://www.wa.gov.au/government/publications/municipal-employees-award-summary "Municipal Employees Award summary"). These awards or parts of them, may not apply if employees are covered by an industrial agreement.

Long service leave entitlements for most local government employees come from the [Local Government (Long Service Leave) Regulations 2024](https://www.legislation.wa.gov.au/legislation/statutes.nsf/law_s48269.html).

Employees should contact the human resources area of your local government, or your union representative for specific queries regarding the Local Government (Long Service Leave) Regulations or other long service leave entitlements provided by an industrial agreement.

### State public sector / Western Australian Government employees

Most state public sector agencies and public sector employees are in the state system.

- Public sector employees with queries about pay rates, working hours, leave and other employment issues should contact the human resources area of their employing agency. If after approaching human resources you are not satisfied, you may wish to contact a grievance officer or follow your agency’s dispute resolution procedure.
- [Coverage of the Long Service Leave Act](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/coverage-of-the-long-service-leave-act "Coverage of the Long Service Leave Act") includes information for state public sector employees _._

### Foreign consulate employees

Whether an employee who works for a foreign state or consulate in Western Australia is covered by the state system will depend on the employee’s residency status and the type of work they perform for the consulate.

In general terms, if a consulate employee is a citizen or permanent resident of Australia and their contract of employment was made in Australia or was to be performed wholly or partly in Australia, then their employment will be covered by the state system.

Different arrangements would apply if the employee is a:

- member of the diplomatic staff of a mission as defined by the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations; or
- consular officer as defined by the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations – for example, the Consul-General.

## National system

The national system covers WA private sector businesses and organisations that are constitutional corporations, as well as some state-owned corporations.

### Private sector businesses and not-for-profit organisations

The national system covers:

- Pty Ltd businesses that are trading or financial corporations.
- Partnerships, where one or more of the partners in the business is a constitutional corporation (trading or financial corporation).
- Trust arrangements, where one or more of the trustees  operating the business is a constitutional corporation (trading or financial corporation).

> _Note – Incorporated employers in the private sector, including Pty Ltd entities, who sell goods or provide services for a fee may satisfy the criteria of a trading or financial corporation._

- Incorporated associations and other not-for-profit organisations, including some sporting clubs and school P&C's which are constitutional corporations (trading or financial corporations) and their employees.
  - A not-for-profit association may be a constitutional corporation if it has sufficiently substantial trading or financial activities, even if the purpose of the organisation is something other than trading or finance or if it receives government funding. Trading activities typically involve buying or selling, and produce revenue for the organisation. Financial activities often involve the borrowing of money and the provision of finance.
  - There is no definitive rule on which system covers these types of organisations and each organisation will need to seek its own legal advice to determine this question, as Wageline is not able to advise on this issue.
- Foreign corporations that are incorporated overseas are automatically constitutional corporations in Australia.

The Fair Work Ombudsman provides information to national system employers and employees on employment conditions (except long service leave and children in employment). Visit [www.fairwork.gov.au](http://www.fairwork.gov.au/) or call the Fair Work Ombudsman on 13 13 94.

Wageline provides information on [long service leave](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/long-service-leave-western-australia "Long service leave in Western Australia") and [when children can work](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/when-children-can-work-western-australia "When children can work in Western Australia") to national system employers and employees.

### Federal public sector / Australian Government employees

All federal public sector agencies and Australian Government employees are in the national system. Contact the human resources area of your employing agency or the Fair Work Ombudsman for employment information.

## Checking system coverage

- Employers - To check whether a business is in the state or national system, private sector employers can:
  - contact their business advisor; or
  - call Wageline on 1300 655 266.
- Employees - To check whether a business is in the state or national system, private sector employees can:
  - ask their employer or a manager;
  - check the employer's business entity name on a pay slip or annual payment summary (group certificate), or in a contract or letter of appointment. The business entity name may be different from the trading name - for example, you may work at the Perth Café (the trading name) but Café Pty Ltd is the legal name of the employer;
  - look up the business on the Australian Government’s Australian Business Number (ABN) lookup website – [www.abr.business.gov.au](https://abr.business.gov.au/). If the business entity name is a trust, you will need to contact Wageline to undertake a more detailed search; or
  - call Wageline on 1300 655 266.

Please read Wageline's disclaimer about searches to check system coverage

[Our disclaimer](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/searches-check-system-coverage "Searches to check system coverage") about how we perform searches using business names.

Some state employment laws apply to national system employers and employees, and some national system provisions apply to the state system. Visit [About the WA state system](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/private-sector-labour-relations/about-the-wa-state-industrial-relations-system "About the WA state industrial relations system") for details.

## Assistance

Need translating and interpreting help to call Wageline? Use the [Translating and Interpreting Service](https://www.tisnational.gov.au/) on 13 14 50 during business hours.

[National Relay Service](https://www.accesshub.gov.au/) helps people who are deaf, hearing and/or speech-impaired contact Wageline. Call the National Relay Service on 13 36 77 and ask to call Wageline on 1300 655 266.
